prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the nearby silver car and person from the much farther road, trees, and cliffs: the car and person are roughly 0.5–2 m from the camera wearer, while most background terrain is approximately 5–30+ m away. In frames 1–3, the person is beside the car’s open rear area and about 0–1 m from the car; both remain close as their image positions shift from right toward the centre, mainly reflecting camera movement or turning. Frame 4 points sharply downward and partly under/alongside the car, placing the car body extremely close above the view and a bag-like object roughly 1–2 m ahead on the ground; much of the person is out of view or occluded. In frame 5, the car and person return on the right, again close to each other and within roughly 1–2 m of the camera wearer; brightness makes near/far ordering clearer than RGB alone, but the smooth, relative monocular depth cannot support precise metre estimates and appears unreliable along silhouettes, open doors, the hatch, and the frame-4 car boundary.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently isolates a car and one person, with a backpack additionally detected near the person in frame 2 and an apparent motorcycle label in frames 3 and 5 that conflicts with the RGB car and is unreliable. Across frames 1–3, the car occupies the left and centre foreground while the person is on its right side, partly overlapping or occluded by the car and about 0–1 m from it; the masks show object extent and overlap more clearly than RGB but provide no dependable metric distance by themselves. Frame 4 is dominated by black background, with only partial car and person masks cut off along the upper edge, showing that both are extremely close and largely outside the downward-facing field of view. By frame 5, the car lies left/centre and the person stands or bends at its right edge, roughly 1–2 m from the camera wearer and within arm’s reach of the car; the person appears oriented toward the open rear area rather than directly toward the camera, although mask geometry alone cannot establish gaze. Mask bleeding between the person and car, missing doors and bags, inconsistent class colours, and the false motorcycle labels make fine spatial boundaries unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map shows one nearby person in frames 1–3 and 5, with no usable body skeleton in frame 4 because the downward-turned view leaves the person mostly cropped or occluded. In frames 1–3, the skeleton moves from left-of-centre toward the centre/right of each frame while remaining roughly 1–2 m away; its bent trunk and arm geometry place the hands in front of and below the upper body, close to the car’s rear area and likely within the person’s arm’s reach. The body orientation is mostly sideways or away from the camera wearer, and the sparse head landmarks do not reliably show eye direction or confirm direct looking toward the camera. In frame 5, the body appears on the right, leaning toward the car with magenta hand detections near the left side of the torso, again placing the hands close to the car; pose makes articulation and reach relationships clearer than RGB alone. Missing joints, fragmented head and hand points, implausible limb connections, and the complete frame-4 failure make exact posture, facing direction, distances, and occlusion boundaries uncertain.
